To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the hippocampal functioning during paradoxical sleep is characterized by: a) depression of the efficiency of polysynaptic pathway from entorhinal cortex to subiculum and back, b) increase in efficiency of monosynaptic pathway from the entorhinal area to pyramids of the CA1 and CA1 areas, c) increase in efficiency and plasticity of the associative connections between pyramids of CA3 area.

during wakefulness and during paradoxical sleep the functioning of the hippocampus is different and that the differences are in accordance with the changes in neuromodulatory activity of the brain during these two behavioral states.

the functioning of the hippocampus during paradoxical sleep differs from that during wakefulness in that the efficiency of polysynaptic connections in the hippocampus is depressed, while the efficiency of monosynaptic connections and of associative connections between pyramids of CA3 area is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of functional significance of the hippocampic system for the brain functioning in wakefulness and paradoxial sleep.
the role of the hippocampus in memory processing during sleep.
the study of the mechanisms of the formation of the paradoxical sleep EEG in the hippocampal area of rabbits and rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
during paradoxical, sleep the hippocampal system is more efficient in the processing of new information, but less efficient in retrieving previously acquired information.

paradoxical sleep is a state of the brain which is characterized by a specific pattern of neuromodulatory influences and by a particular pattern of changes in the efficiency of synaptic transmission in different neuronal circuits.

paradoxical sleep is characterized by the following changes: (i) a decrease in efficacy of polysynaptic pathway in the hippocampus; (ii) an increase in efficacy of the perforante path input to the pyramids of CA3 and CA1 areas and of the associative connections between CA2-3 neurones; (iii) a decrease in the efficiency of the polysynaptic connections in the hippocampal circuit and (iv) a decrease in efficiency of the hippocampally generated theta rhythm
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hippocampus during paradoxical sleep is in a state of enhanced plasticity and that this state is due to changes in the levels of several neuroactive substances.
during paradoxical (or REM) sleep the hippocampal system operates as a "filter" for information processing, which can be compared to a "black hole" in the universe.
the hippocampal polysynaptic pathway is the main target of the neuromodulatory influences during paradoxical sleep.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hippocampal circuit is not just a memory storehouse, but also a mechanism for the generation of novel memories.
we have developed a new approach for studying the effects of sleep on the hippocampus, which allows to study the effects of sleep deprivation on memory.

we have shown the importance of the role of the hippocampus in the control of the paradoxical sleep, and that the hippocampus can be used as a target for pharmacological interventions in sleep disorders.
